_readme: A suppression turns one rule off for one route. It never turns off a rule file-wide,
and it never turns off a rule for every route -- that is what deleting the rule is for,
and deleting it is at least visible in a diff.
reason is REQUIRED and is itself validated (SS-001). A suppression with no reason is an
error, because an unexplained suppression is indistinguishable from a bug someone got
tired of. Say what makes this route the exception, not that the rule is annoying.
Seeded empty on purpose: the Phase 2 failure list is meant to be read, not silenced.
FIRST ENTRY ADDED 2026-08-26, and it is worth saying why it is not a retreat from that.
SS-204 could have shipped as a warning instead, with a comment asking someone to promote
it later. A suppression here is strictly stronger: the rule runs at error severity for
every other route from day one, the exception is named and dated and reasoned, and
deleting it is forced by the work that unblocks it. A downgrade would have protected

suppressions.reason: The visible date reads "Last updated: January 22, 2026" against a newest content commit of 2026-08-26, and SS-204 is right about that. It cannot be fixed by editing the date: the policy text does not yet describe what the two forms actually collect, where submissions are stored, how long they are kept, or how a deletion request is honoured, and stamping today onto unamended text would assert a currency the document does not have -- the same lie in the other direction. The amendment is drafted and blocked on two things: running scripts/expertise-purge.mjs --confirm (no Netlify credentials on the authoring machine), and confirming no submitted address was ever added to a mailing list. DELETE THIS ENTRY IN THE COMMIT THAT PUBLISHES THE AMENDMENT -- that is what makes removing it a required step rather than a remembered one.
